question: When may GA display a progression's catalog Category as metadata, and what further evidence would support a claim about the style of a performed recording?
production_path: investigation: observe hypothesize test conclude reflect
source reading: pin GA catalog and domain record revision
test: cross_validate lesson fields, counts, and five answers against pinned sources
hypothesis: A lesson that distinguishes stored progression labels from observed performances can make GA's style captions useful without presenting catalog associations as independently verified history or listening evidence.
evidence: At GA commit dc2e74cbd992a298f67efb928b5b3754615e1924, Common/GA.Business.Config/ChordProgressions.yaml gives ii-V-I Category Jazz, C Major, RomanNumerals ii7/V7/I, and Chords Dm7/G7/Cmaj7.
The pinned YAML gives 12-Bar Blues Category Blues and twelve chord positions E/E/E/E/A/A/E/E/B/A/E/B, while its AAB lyrical Structure is a descriptive field without lyrics or audio in the record.
The pinned Rhythm Changes entry says AABA and gives ASection Bb/Gm/Cm/F and BSection D/G/Cm/F, but has no top-level Chords or RomanNumerals list and no performance timing.

The pinned I-vi-IV-V record contains a vi-IV-I-V variation with Am/F/C/G and Context Pop ballad version but no variation Category. A separate top-level vi–IV–I–V (Pop Loop) record has Category Pop and the same chords; two records within one catalog are not independent performance evidence.

At the same GA commit, Common/GA.Domain.Core/Theory/Harmony/Progressions/ProgressionCorpusItem.cs declares required StyleLabel and Source strings and a Chords list defaulting to empty. The source does not establish a YAML-to-corpus mapping or independently validate style labels.

The English draft has five answered source-based exercises. No recording, score, listener trial, or classifier was analyzed. Research duration was not instrumented; duration_seconds=0 records that limitation.
